item.turbines.pressured_iron_ingot.toolt: A pressure-treated iron material used to build turbine and Hydro components.
Craft it from six Create Iron Sheets. Crushing it with Crushing Wheels yields Pressured Iron Dust.
item.turbines.pressured_iron_dust.toolti: Powdered pressure-treated iron used to make Pressured Sand.
Crush Pressured Iron Ingots with Crushing Wheels, then smelt the dust into Pressured Sand.
item.turbines.pearlescent_dew_bucket.too: A hyper-energetic alchemical fluid that burns at extreme temperatures. Only Steam Boilers have the refractory capacity to contain its heat so most engines would melt down instantly.
Burns at heat level 4.0, exceeding superheated limits. Consumes very slowly. Only compatible with the Steam Boiler and incompatible with other engines and blaze burners.
block.turbines.steam_boiler.tooltip.summ: Produces Steam which can be fed to Steam Turbines, Steam Pumps, Steam Compressors, and Pressurized Steam Pipes. Make sure to feed it fuel and water!
block.turbines.steam_boiler.tooltip.beha: It can consume liquid fuels too. Pearlescent Dew is the best fuel source for the Steam Boiler. Feed water and liquid fuel through pipes or from buckets, and supply solid fuels with mechanical arms.

Recommended layout: place a Steam Pump directly after the boiler, a Steam Compressor after the pump, then Steam Turbines afterwards, further down the line. Place Pressurized Pipes between the boiler and pump if you want to combine multiple boilers into a unit/cluster.
block.turbines.pressure_pipe.tooltip.sum: Holds Steam for other machines. Use it along with a Pressurized Steam Pump to move steam between machines together.
block.turbines.pressure_pipe.tooltip.beh: The pipes do not move steam on their own. Use a Steam Pump to move steam through them.
Uses rotational force supplied on the sides to compress Steam to have higher pressure and throughput. Place it after either a Steam Pump.
Pressure and throughput scale with the rotational RPM, and the kinetic stress impact obviously increases the higher the RPM goes.
Outputs to any other machine that accepts steam input, like the Steam Turbine and Steam Jet Thruster.
block.turbines.steam_turbine.tooltip.sum: Consumes Steam to generate power which is sent to the Steam Turbine Shaft. You can chain 10 of these together for higher SU.
block.turbines.steam_turbine.tooltip.beh: More pressure and throughput = more power produced and more turbines you can chain. Steam weakens as it moves between turbines, so 10 chained turbines is the max before the Steam Turbine Shaft.
You can view the stats of these with engineer goggles.
block.turbines.turbine_shaft.tooltip.sum: Generates SU from chained Steam Turbines.
block.turbines.turbine_shaft.tooltip.beh: The turbine shaft calculates turbine count, pressure, and throughput for the total SU output. Increasing these = more SU.
Steam is exhausted on the side too!
block.turbines.steam_pump.tooltip.summar: Pulls steam from all connected Pressurized Steam Pipes and machines that output steam into one direction.
block.turbines.steam_pump.tooltip.behavi: The Pump has an adjustable Pump Rate. Increasing this also increases the Kinetic Stress Impact, and higher RPM increases the Stress Impact as well.
Pump Rate and RPM control steam transfer speed. Higher values transfer steam faster.
block.turbines.steam_jet_thruster.toolti: Consumes Steam to produce directed thrust. Connect a compressor along with a pump for increased efficiency and power.
block.turbines.steam_ejector.tooltip.sum: Consumes Steam to pump fluids up to 80 blocks away at 10 pressure and 3 Steam/t. Lower pressure or throughput reduces range, but transfer speed stays at 1 bucket per second.
block.turbines.large_turbine.tooltip.sum: A horizontal rotor stage designed for Hydro Turbine chambers with 1 to 10 vertical stages.
block.turbines.large_turbine.tooltip.beh: Stack 1 to 10 Large Turbines vertically inside the Hydro chamber. Center each stage in a 5×5 layer, keeping the surrounding 3×3 interior clear of solid blocks.

Use a source-water pool or connect any Create fluid network. For full output, the pool targets 9 source blocks per stage or the network must continuously supply 2,000 mB/s (100 mB/t). Lower supply reduces SU proportionally.
The top stage runs at full speed and each stage below it runs five percent slower. A fully supplied 10-stage unit can reach 2,000,000 SU at 256 RPM.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.tooltip.summa: Validates a Hydro chamber and outputs kinetic power from its Large Turbine stages.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.tooltip.behav: Use Engineer's Goggles to check the requirements: 1 to 10 vertical stages, a Large Turbine centered in each layer, clear space around each stage, valid walls and caps, one Inlet, and one Exhaust.
Place it in a roof or floor opening, facing outward. You can install one or both; two shafts share the unit's output.
Output scales with stages and water supplied. A 10-stage unit with a full source pool or a steady 2,000 mB/s network supply can reach 2,000,000 SU at 256 RPM.
One Hydro Turbine IO acts as the Inlet when facing up or the Exhaust when facing down.

Place it in the roof facing up. It draws source water from above or accepts water from any connected Create fluid network. Network mode consumes up to 100 mB/t (2,000 mB/s) from its 3,000 mB temporary buffer; a tank is not required.

Place it in the floor facing down. Connect Create pipes or pumps to recover its buffered water, or put a Steam Boiler directly below. With no receiver it places a water source every 5 seconds; a full buffer blocks the unit.
Transparent, blast-resistant glass for Hydro chamber walls.
Use it as a transparent wall block around the 3×3 Hydro chamber interior. Chamber corners may be left open.
It has stone-like hardness and iron-block blast resistance. It drops without Silk Touch.
block.turbines.pressured_sand.tooltip.su: Falling sand made by smelting Pressured Iron Dust. Smelt it again to make Reinforced Glass.
Connect a Create fluid network supplying water continuously. It must deliver 100 mB/t (2,000 mB/s) for full power.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.goggles.title: Hydro Shaft:
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.goggles.struc: Make sure the chamber is built correctly. Its blocks do not pass the structure check.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.goggles.sourc: Source water: %s / %s blocks for full SU
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.goggles.netwo: Connect a Create fluid network supplying water continuously. It must deliver 100 mB/t (2,000 mB/s) for full power.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.sta: Stack 1 to 10 Large Turbine stages vertically.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.cle: Keep the 3×3 area around each turbine free of solid blocks; air or water is fine.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.wal: Build the 5×5 side walls from Reinforced Glass or full, nonflammable blocks at least as hard as stone; corners may be open.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.roo: Use full, opaque, nonflammable roof blocks; nonflammable bottom-half slabs at least as hard as stone are allowed here. Leave the shaft and Inlet openings.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.flo: Use full, opaque, nonflammable floor blocks. Slabs are not allowed on the floor. Leave the shaft and Exhaust openings.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.io: Place one Hydro Turbine IO facing up at the roof and one facing down at the floor.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.checklist.sha: Place a Hydro Shaft at the top, bottom, or both; the top faces up and the bottom faces down.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.not_lo: I can't check this part yet. Load the whole chamber and try again.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.missin: Add a Hydro Shaft at the top or bottom of the chamber.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.shaft_: Turn the Hydro Shaft so it faces straight up or down.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.too_ma: Use no more than 10 Large Turbine stages.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.missin: Add 1 to 10 Large Turbines in a vertical stack beside the Hydro Shaft.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.dual_s: If both shafts are installed, point the top one up and the bottom one down.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.missin: Place one Hydro Turbine IO at the roof, facing up for the Inlet.
Place one Hydro Turbine IO at the floor, facing down for the Exhaust.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.roof_b: The roof needs full, opaque, nonflammable blocks. Nonflammable bottom-half slabs at least as hard as stone are allowed here; leave the shaft and Inlet openings.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.floor_: The floor needs full, opaque, nonflammable blocks. Slabs are not allowed on the floor; leave the shaft and Exhaust openings.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.stage_: Side walls need full, nonflammable blocks at least as hard as stone, or Reinforced Glass. Keep the 3×3 middle clear; corners can be open.
block.turbines.hydro_shaft.status.water_: Water is available; output scales with water.
Add water above the Inlet or connect a Create fluid network.
block.turbines.lava_duct_turbine.tooltip: Generates SU based on how many sides are touching lava. Each side touching lava produces 475 SU. Place below a Lava Duct Shaft and stack multiple turbines up to 5 max.
block.turbines.lava_duct_shaft.tooltip.s: Collects SU from Lava Duct Turbines placed below it. Outputs kinetic power and requires continuous water supply to its copper pipe side.
block.turbines.directional_analog_gearsh: A directional gearshift controlled by analog redstone signals. The LEFT and RIGHT sides determine output speed and direction from their signal differential.
Output speed follows the input direction with an RPM modifier based on the redstone differential. Higher differential = higher speed.
Output direction is locked to an absolute direction determined by which redstone side is stronger. The input direction is completely ignored; only the speed magnitude is used.
Kinetic input must be supplied from the BACK side (Marked Red). The OPPOSITE side (Marked Blue) is the output.
block.turbines.network_diagnoser.tooltip: Displays network RPM, SU usage, and allows stress testing. Right-click to configure.
Shows live RPM and stress data from the connected kinetic network when viewed with engineer goggles.
When active, injects configurable stress into the network to test capacity limits.
